variables.reason: The typed ledger defines Ra as "the first-order absolute moment of height fluctuations, representing a characteristic roughness height." The KB record pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness explicitly defines the arithmetic mean roughness (aliases: first-order moment of height fluctuations) and lists si_dimension: L and si_unit: m, directly matching the ledger definition and confirming that Ra carries the SI length dimension. The cited record therefore supports all known coordinates (L=1, all others 0) in the proposed vector.

The ledger labels kt as "the peak-to-valley height of the roughness profile." The KB record pq_peak_to_valley_height defines mean peak-to-valley roughness height and states its si_dimension: L (unit m), explicitly matching the ledger meaning as a height difference. This record supports the proposed vector (L=1, others 0).

The ledger defines k_rms as "the root-mean-square height of the roughness profile." The KB record pq_rms_roughness_height defines root-mean-square roughness height, with si_dimension: L and si_unit: m, directly corresponding to the ledger variable and confirming the length dimension (L=1).

The ledger describes Sk as "the skewness of roughness height fluctuations, a dimensionless statistical moment." The KB record pq_height_skewness defines surface-height skewness as the third standardized moment and gives si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). That record directly applies to the ledger Sk and supports all coordinates (all zeros) of the proposed vector.

The ledger gives Ku as "the kurtosis of roughness height fluctuations, a dimensionless statistical moment." The KB record pq_height_kurtosis defines surface-height kurtosis as the fourth standardized moment and lists si_dimension: 1, matching the ledger definition and supporting the all-zero SI exponent vector.

The ledger states ES is "the effective streamwise slope of the roughness, a dimensionless geometric parameter." The KB record pq_effective_surface_slope defines effective surface slope as a mean absolute gradient (derivative of height over horizontal distance) and notes a surface-height derivative is length/length and therefore dimensionless (si_dimension: 1). This record applies directly to ES and supports the all-zero SI exponent vector.

The ledger defines Po as "the surface porosity, a dimensionless fraction representing void area ratio." The KB record pq_porosity defines porosity (surface porosity) as a fraction with si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless) and explicitly cautions to confirm the geometric definition; it nonetheless confirms the variable is dimensionless. The record thus supports the all-zero SI exponent vector.

The dimensionless output ks/Ra is derived from these inputs, consistent with dimensional analysis principles.
